h1: How a Furniture Showroom Can Grow Sales from Ads 2.5x by Optimising for Visits
quickAnswer: In this benchmark scenario, a solid-wood furniture showroom spending ₹75,000 a month replaces discount ads with workshop Reels, qualifies leads on WhatsApp by room, budget and timeline, and offers a free design consultation at the showroom. Showroom visits from ads rise from 12 to 34 a month and sales from ₹3.4 lakh to ₹8.5 lakh.
cardSummary: Showroom visits from digital nearly tripled, and monthly sales from ads grew from ₹3.4 lakh to ₹8.5 lakh at the same budget.

businessPattern.type: Single large showroom with an in-house workshop; premium and value ranges
businessPattern.location: Fast-growing residential suburb of a metro city
businessPattern.salesCycle: 2–8 weeks; usually 1–2 showroom visits before buying

challenge: "People message asking for the price list and disappear. The ones who come to the showroom buy — we just can't get enough of them through the door." Ads promoted discounts to a broad audience, so most leads were price-shoppers. There was no way to tell which ads produced visits or sales.
objectives: Raise the share of qualified leads (budget, timeline, location fit)
Turn more qualified leads into showroom visits
Measure sales from ads, not just leads

whatWeDid.title: Craft-led video
whatWeDid.body: Workshop Reels showing timber selection, joinery and finishing — giving buyers a reason to pay for quality rather than chase the lowest price.

whatWeDid.title: Qualifying WhatsApp flow
whatWeDid.body: Leads chose the room, budget band and move-in timeline before receiving a catalogue; hot leads were called within the hour.

whatWeDid.title: Visit-first offer
whatWeDid.body: Instead of a discount, a free home-measurement and design consultation booked during the showroom visit.

whatWeDid.title: Google Search for high intent
whatWeDid.body: Campaigns on "teak wood bed [city]" and "furniture showroom near me", plus Google Maps visibility with directions and showroom photos.

whatWeDid.title: Closed-loop tracking
whatWeDid.body: Every lead got a WhatsApp ID that the showroom team marked as visited and sold, so cost per sale could be calculated by campaign.

whatMadeTheDifference: Optimising for the showroom visit, not the lead. Furniture is bought after people touch and sit on it. Filtering price-shoppers early and giving serious buyers a reason to visit lifted sales even though total leads grew only modestly.

faqs.question: How can a furniture store get more showroom visits?
faqs.answer: Qualify leads before sharing prices, then give serious buyers a reason to visit — such as a free measurement or design consultation — instead of a discount. Keep Google Maps directions and photos current.

faqs.question: Are Meta ads good for furniture businesses?
faqs.answer: Yes, for showing craftsmanship and reaching nearby homeowners. Pair them with Google Search for high-intent queries like "furniture showroom near me".

faqs.question: Why do furniture leads go cold?
faqs.answer: Most early enquiries are price checks. A short WhatsApp flow asking room, budget and move-in date separates buyers from browsers, and fast calls to hot leads keep them warm.

faqs.question: How should a furniture brand measure ad results?
faqs.answer: Track each lead through to showroom visit and sale. Cost per sale and return on ad spend matter more than cost per lead for high-ticket purchases.
